# Palette: viridis for the primary scale, magma for the second one.
v_dark <- "#440154"; v_blue <- "#31688e"; v_teal <- "#21918c"; v_green <- "#5ec962"
m_pink <- "#b73779"; m_purple <- "#8c2981"; m_orange <- "#fc8961"
mse <- function(y, pred) mean((y - pred)^2)
pin <- function(u, tau) u * (tau - (u < 0))   # the pinball loss
# NHANES (data note: data/nhanes.md): adults with every column used here recorded, split at random
# 4,000 training, 3,000 tuning; the rest is the test set, used once, to check multicalibration.
nh <- NHANESraw |>
  filter(Age >= 20) |>
  select(Diabetes, Gender, Age, Race1, Poverty, Weight, Height, BMI, Pulse, BPSysAve, TotChol, DirectChol, PhysActive) |>
  drop_na() |>
  mutate(diabetes = as.numeric(Diabetes == "Yes"), male = as.numeric(Gender == "male"),
         active = as.numeric(PhysActive == "Yes"))
set.seed(310)   # the deck's one seed: the split, then every random step below, in order
nh_id <- sample(nrow(nh))
nh_train <- nh[nh_id[1:4000], ]
nh_tune  <- nh[nh_id[4001:7000], ]
nh_test  <- nh[nh_id[7001:nrow(nh)], ]
# Simulated data for parts 1 and 2, the same as the note's: noise that grows with x.
f_sim <- function(x) 3 + x + 2 * sin(x)
s_sim <- function(x) 0.5 + 0.35 * x
sim <- function(n) tibble(x = runif(n, 0, 10)) |> mutate(y = f_sim(x) + s_sim(x) * rnorm(n))
het_train <- sim(1000)
het_fresh <- sim(2000)
x_grid <- tibble(x = seq(0, 10, length.out = 201))
# The causality lecture's diagram of the adjustment theorem.
dag_adjust <- function(intervened = FALSE, title = NULL) {
  s <- if (intervened) '{ Z [pos="1,1"] T [pos="0,0"] Y [pos="2,0"] Z -> Y T -> Y }' else
                       '{ Z [pos="1,1"] T [pos="0,0"] Y [pos="2,0"] Z -> T Z -> Y T -> Y }'
  dag(s) %>% tidy_dagitty() %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend)) +
    geom_dag_point(size = 15, colour = "#e5ecf6") +
    geom_dag_text(size = 8, colour = v_dark) +
    geom_dag_edges(edge_width = 1.3) +
    expand_limits(x = c(-0.35, 2.35), y = c(-0.4, 1.45)) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    labs(title = title) +
    theme_dag_blank() +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 15, hjust = 0.5, colour = v_dark))
}
# The explanatory causal model of part 5, drawn by hand in the convention of Loftus, Bynum and Hansen (2024),
# Figure 5: one graph with the outcome y and the prediction y-hat (boxed); solid arrows for relations in the
# world, dashed arrows from the model's inputs to the prediction, curved so that they cross no node.
ecm_plot <- function() {
  arw <- arrow(length = unit(0.13, "inches"), type = "closed")
  solid <- tribble(~x, ~y, ~xend, ~yend,          # x1 -> x2, x1 -> y, x2 -> y, x1 -> x3, y -> x3
    0.29, 1.15, 1.71, 1.95,   0.33, 1, 3.67, 1,   2.29, 1.95, 3.71, 1.15,   0.29, 0.85, 1.71, 0.05,   3.71, 0.85, 2.29, 0.05)
  ggplot() +
    geom_segment(data = solid, aes(x, y, xend = xend, yend = yend), colour = v_dark, linewidth = 1.1, arrow = arw) +
    annotate("curve", x = 2.32, y = -0.2, xend = 5.05, yend = -0.85, colour = m_pink, linewidth = 1.1, linetype = "dashed",
             curvature = 0.12, arrow = arw) +
    annotate("curve", x = 0, y = 0.64, xend = 5.0, yend = -1.05, colour = m_pink, linewidth = 1.1, linetype = "dashed",
             curvature = 0.42, angle = 90, arrow = arw) +
    annotate("curve", x = 2.34, y = 2.15, xend = 5.4, yend = -0.55, colour = m_pink, linewidth = 1.1, linetype = "dashed",
             curvature = -0.55, angle = 90, arrow = arw) +
    geom_label(data = tibble(x = c(0, 2, 4, 2), y = c(1, 2.1, 1, -0.1), lab = c("x[1]", "x[2]", "y", "x[3]")),
               aes(x, y, label = lab), parse = TRUE, size = 7, linewidth = 0.3, label.padding = unit(0.35, "lines")) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 5.1, xmax = 5.7, ymin = -1.2, ymax = -0.6, fill = "white", colour = "black", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.6) +
    annotate("text", x = 5.4, y = -0.9, label = "hat(y)", parse = TRUE, size = 7) +
    coord_equal(xlim = c(-0.4, 5.9), ylim = c(-1.75, 2.5), clip = "off") + theme_void()
}

# Part 2: a line with constant noise, lm's 90% prediction interval, the points outside it highlighted.
bg2 <- tibble(x = runif(400, 0, 10)) |> mutate(y = 1 + 0.5 * x + rnorm(400))
bg2_fit <- lm(y ~ x, bg2)
bg2_band <- tibble(x = seq(0, 10, length.out = 101)) |>
  bind_cols(as_tibble(predict(bg2_fit, tibble(x = seq(0, 10, length.out = 101)), interval = "prediction", level = 0.9)))
bg2_pi <- predict(bg2_fit, bg2, interval = "prediction", level = 0.9)
bg2$out <- bg2$y < bg2_pi[, "lwr"] | bg2$y > bg2_pi[, "upr"]
bg_save(ggplot(bg2, aes(x, y)) + geom_ribbon(data = bg2_band, aes(x, ymin = lwr, ymax = upr), inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "#fde725", alpha = 0.3) +

# Part 5: the ECM for the protein-signalling data of Sachs et al. (2005), as drawn by Loftus, Bynum and Hansen
# (2024), Figure 5 (left): PKA and its descendants in bold; blue, the paths from PKA; dashed, the model's inputs.
sachs_nodes <- tribble(~name, ~x, ~y, ~bold,
  "PKC", 2, 4, FALSE, "pjnk", 3.5, 4, FALSE, "P38", 0.5, 3, TRUE, "praf", 2, 3, TRUE, "pmek", 3.5, 3, TRUE,
  "plcg", 0.5, 2, FALSE, "PKA", 2, 2, TRUE, "p44/42", 3.5, 2, FALSE, "pakts473", 2, 1.3, TRUE,
  "PIP2", 0.5, 0.6, FALSE, "PIP3", 2, 0.6, FALSE, "hat", 3.5, 0.6, FALSE)
sachs_edge <- function(from, to, kind, a = 0.22, b = 0.26) {
  f <- sachs_nodes[sachs_nodes$name == from, ]; t <- sachs_nodes[sachs_nodes$name == to, ]
  len <- sqrt((t$x - f$x)^2 + (t$y - f$y)^2)
  tibble(x = f$x + a * (t$x - f$x) / len, y = f$y + a * (t$y - f$y) / len,
         xend = t$x - b * (t$x - f$x) / len, yend = t$y - b * (t$y - f$y) / len, kind = kind)
}
sachs_solid <- bind_rows(
  sachs_edge("PKC", "pjnk", "world", 0.45, 0.4), sachs_edge("PKC", "P38", "world"), sachs_edge("PKC", "praf", "world"),
  sachs_edge("PKC", "pmek", "world"), sachs_edge("plcg", "PKC", "world"), sachs_edge("PIP2", "PKC", "world"),
  sachs_edge("PKA", "pjnk", "world"), sachs_edge("PKA", "p44/42", "world", 0.45, 0.5), sachs_edge("pmek", "p44/42", "world"),
  sachs_edge("plcg", "PIP2", "world"), sachs_edge("PIP3", "PIP2", "world", 0.4, 0.4), sachs_edge("PIP3", "pakts473", "world", 0.2, 0.2),
  sachs_edge("PKA", "P38", "pka"), sachs_edge("PKA", "praf", "pka"), sachs_edge("PKA", "pmek", "pka"),
  sachs_edge("PKA", "pakts473", "pka", 0.2, 0.2), sachs_edge("praf", "pmek", "pka", 0.45, 0.5))
sachs_dashed <- bind_rows(sachs_edge("P38", "hat", "pka", 0.35, 0.35) |> mutate(curv = 0.12),
  sachs_edge("praf", "hat", "pka", 0.3, 0.35) |> mutate(curv = 0.1), sachs_edge("pmek", "hat", "pka", 0.3, 0.35) |> mutate(curv = -0.35),
  sachs_edge("pakts473", "hat", "pka", 0.35, 0.45) |> mutate(curv = 0.05), sachs_edge("PKA", "hat", "direct", 0.35, 0.35) |> mutate(curv = 0.2))
sachs_arw <- arrow(length = unit(0.09, "inches"), type = "closed")
sachs_cols <- c(world = "white", pka = "#8fd3ff", direct = m_orange)
p5 <- ggplot() +
  geom_segment(data = sachs_solid, aes(x, y, xend = xend, yend = yend, colour = kind), linewidth = 0.7, arrow = sachs_arw) +
  annotate("curve", x = 2.25, y = 0.72, xend = 0.62, yend = 1.78, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.7, curvature = -0.3, arrow = sachs_arw)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(sachs_dashed))) p5 <- p5 +
  geom_curve(data = sachs_dashed[i, ], aes(x, y, xend = xend, yend = yend, colour = kind), linewidth = 0.8,
             linetype = "dashed", curvature = sachs_dashed$curv[i], arrow = sachs_arw)
p5 <- p5 +
  geom_text(data = filter(sachs_nodes, name != "hat"), aes(x, y, label = name, fontface = if_else(bold, "bold", "plain")),
            colour = "white", size = 7, family = "serif") +
  annotate("text", x = 3.5, y = 0.6, label = 'widehat("p44/42")', parse = TRUE, colour = "white", size = 7, family = "serif") +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 3.05, xmax = 3.95, ymin = 0.33, ymax = 0.9, fill = NA, colour = "white", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = sachs_cols, guide = "none") +
  coord_fixed(ratio = 1, xlim = c(-3.4, 4.15), ylim = c(0.1, 4.35), expand = FALSE) + bg_void
bg_save(p5, "part5-sachs-ecm.png")

## Where we left off {minutes="3"}

::: {.notes}
QUESTION: which loss makes the best prediction the 90th percentile?

The title slide's question first (its minutes are counted here), then this table, then the box.
:::

| Loss | Best prediction at $x$ | |
|---|---|---|
| Squared error, $(y - \hat y)^2$ | the conditional mean, $\mathbb E[Y \mid X = x]$ | optimal model theorem |
| Absolute error, $\lvert y - \hat y \rvert$ | the conditional median | stated |
| A miss costs $c_{FN}$, a false alarm $c_{FP}$ | predict $1$ when $p(x) > c^\star = \frac{c_{FP}}{c_{FP} + c_{FN}}$ | optimal threshold theorem |

**Decision principle**: choose the prediction $\hat y$ that minimizes the expected loss given the inputs, $\mathbb E[\ell(Y, \hat y) \mid X = x]$

::: {.ask}
Squared loss gives the mean, absolute loss the median. Which loss makes the best prediction the 90th percentile?
:::
